exposure: Presence of jellyfish sign (JS) on cervical sonography
outcome: Risk of maternal morbidity in cases of abnormally invasive placenta (AIP) previa totalis
Accuracy of JS in diagnosing AIP
Admission to postoperative intensive care unit (ICU)
cohort: 39 singleton pregnancies with placenta previa totalis
finding: The presence of the jellyfish sign (JS) on cervical sonography was significantly associated with increased maternal morbidity in cases of abnormally invasive placenta (AIP) previa totalis, including higher blood loss, transfusions, ICU admissions, and cesarean hysterectomy rates.
